Verification wasn't just static reading: the wage-core and money-surfaces slices extracted the pure math (hourlyRate/shiftGross/computeNet/sanitizeData) into a scratch Node module and replayed it against concrete cases (empty period, 8h shift, a 220-case rounding-drift scan that found 24 hits, 0×-multiplier pricing, percent-withholding preview gap), and pattern-lab replayed patternMetrics/planPatternApply against all 5 presets plus custom cycles. worst: wage-math-00 (confirmed, medium, wageCore:true): the hero's "Taxes & deductions" chip renders `calc.ded` — the uncapped deduction total — while computeNet caps pre/post-tax deductions for the number it actually uses to produce take-home, and the Breakdown modal one tap away shows the capped rows. Whenever flat custom withholdings exceed gross, the three numbers a nurse sees on the primary screen (Gross, Taxes chip, Take-home) stop being arithmetically consistent with each other and with the Breakdown she'd tap into to double-check — in the app whose entire premise is "trust this number before you work the shift," the hero disagreeing with its own drill-down is the most damaging single defect in this lens.
toReachEight: Fix the 6 confirmed mediums, prioritizing the ones that silently misprice or misrepresent a real dollar figure rather than just a display nit: wage-math-00 (hero chip vs. Breakdown disagreement), wage-math-01 (blanked/garbage multiplier silently zeroing a shift's differential pay), and wage-math-12 (Add-Shift defaulting to 'night' and pricing a differential the nurse switched off — this recurs as cross-surface-01 and product-design-00-adjacent findings, so it's a systemic keepRatio/active-flag gap, not an isolated bug). Then wage-math-06 (paystub import inventing a negative differential), wage-math-09 and wage-math-10 (pattern lab presenting an average or a wrong-priced brush cell as a certain, specific number with no on-screen qualifier) — all six go through the wage-core skill's protocol (baseline probes, a new assertion per fix, the deployed-build equality check) since every one touches Invariant-3-adjacent code. The 9 low findings are real but lower priority; clearing even half of them (especially wage-math-02's independent chip rounding and wage-math-04/13's keepRatio-vs-computeNet drift, which several other lenses converge on too) would help but isn't required to clear the bar. ranAgainst: All 5 slices security owns (per docs/council.md's matrix) were examined in the 2026-09-13 run: swap-board (migrations 001 in full, every swap RPC/client call in index.html, live column-grant/RLS/policy checks against project mnnlgcxnvodjwlhhiphq, GitHub visibility), data-sync (sanitizeData, saveToSupabase, hydrateFromCloud, the 15s poll, migration 000, live pg_constraint/pg_policies on user_data), calendar-sync (ical-proxy/index.ts in full plus live probes against the deployed function, migration 002, the .ics export/import path, serializeState never carrying icalUrl), telemetry-auth (boot-script error capture, createClient/OAuth flow, track/trackDeferred, live pg_constraint CHECKs on events/feedback, auth-js flowType source inspection, sandbox Chromium checks of the implicit-flow hash behavior), and infra (all 4 migrations, ci.yml/deploy.yml, check_build.mjs, tests/harness.mjs+smoke.mjs, SRI/CSP, live GitHub ruleset state). Findings were then adversarially refuted, not just asserted.
worst: security-00 (critical, confirmed): poster_key on the swap board is reversible — live-verified column grants let any co-member read other members' user_id and the group creator's id, and the derivation salt ('scrubpay-swaps') is a hardcoded string in a public repo. This defeats the swap board's core, explicitly-designed promise (Invariant 7, docs/swap-board.md's audited anonymity model) with nothing exotic required — just reading columns the app already grants. Compounding it, security-01 (high, confirmed) means propose_swap has no membership check at all, so any group member can reserve/hide arbitrary posts, and security-05 (high, confirmed) means the free-tier database has no server-side size bound on user_data — MAX_BLOB_BYTES is a client-only check any signed-in account can bypass to fill shared infrastructure. Six more mediums are confirmed on top of that (RLS-policy bypass stranding swap state, unvalidated cross-user write in doApplyPlan, ical-proxy accepting any anon-key holder rather than a real signed-in user, a stale feed URL surviving sign-out onto the next account's session, Google sign-in using the implicit OAuth flow instead of PKCE, and a client_error batch that can silently exceed the live DB CHECK constraint and get dropped after the ring buffer is already cleared).
toReachEight: At minimum: close security-00 (stop granting anon/authenticated direct SELECT on swap_members/swap_groups columns that leak user_id, or move co-member visibility behind a security-definer function that never returns raw ids; treat the salt as compromised and plan rotation) and security-01 (add the leg-membership check propose_swap is missing) — both are live, exploitable defects in a feature the docs already call out as audited and safe, so shipping with them confirmed-open is the single biggest gap between this score and 8. Then close security-05 (a DB-level CHECK or trigger bounding user_data.data size — the client-only guard is not a guard), security-02/03 (RLS policy fix for raw match-decline, and validation on doApplyPlan's cross-user write), security-08/09 (require a real user context in ical-proxy, clear icalUrl/icalSub state on sign-out), security-11 (switch Supabase auth to PKCE explicitly), and security-12 (cap or chunk the client_error batch to the live 2000-byte column constraint before clearing the ring buffer). After those 9 confirmed findings are fixed and re-verified (ideally with the swap-board RLS audit script finally ported into tests/ per the Open Items note, so this class of regression is caught mechanically rather than by the next council run), the low-severity backlog (security-04, 06, 07, 10, 13, 14) is what would remain to actually clear a full 10.

ranAgainst:
The mobile-ux lens owns 7 of the council's 13 slices, by the matrix's own design (docs/council.md): money-surfaces, calendar, add-shift, pattern-lab, onboarding, settings-etc, swap-board. All 7 were actually examined per docs/council-runs/2026-09-13/ranAgainst.json, and the methodology was substantive, not eyeballed: money-surfaces and add-shift were driven live (harness rebuilt, real iPhone-13-profile Chromium via Playwright, getBoundingClientRect/getComputedStyle measurements and a screenshot of the hero card, not inference from CSS); calendar, pattern-lab, onboarding, settings-etc and swap-board were verified by reading the full component + CSS and computing box-model/tap-target arithmetic by hand from the literal values, cross-checked against the app's own established conventions (e.g. .acct-menu button and .pl-brushes .chip-sel's 44px). The other 6 slices (boot, wage-core, data-sync, calendar-sync, telemetry-auth, infra) are out of this lens's scope by the council's own design — other lenses (code-quality, security, performance) own those — so their absence is not a coverage gap here.

Findings basis: 14 total findings, 11 confirmed after adversarial review (1 high, 10 medium) plus 3 low-severity/not-agent-verified backlog items, spread across all 7 owned slices with no slice coming back clean.
worst: A single systemic pattern — controls sized well under the app's own established 44px tap-target convention — recurs across nearly every owned slice (Settings dollar-amount fields at 17px tall, the calendar pay-period chip at ~19px, Add-Shift SHIFT TYPE chips 5px short, Pattern Lab grid cells, est-banner buttons, the avatar (the *sole* mobile route to Settings/Sign-out) at 40px with no hit-slop, and a savings-goal "Del" button at ~35x34px sitting directly beside an editable field with no confirmation dialog — unlike its sibling differential-delete, so a thumb that lands a few px off the amount field permanently deletes a goal with no undo). On top of that, a high-severity defect sits on the very first screen a nurse sees: the hero card's two footer links (mobile-ux-00) accidentally inherit the full `.hero` card style via a class-name collision, live-verified to add ~120px of dead scroll and render as broken-looking dark pills instead of text links — this is the app's own centerpiece surface, not an edge case. None of this is individually catastrophic (nothing crashes, the app remains usable one-handed), but for a lens whose whole mandate is "one-handed, mid-shift, on an iPhone," finding the tap-target convention violated in essentially every reviewed component, plus a visual defect on the landing screen, plus one live data-loss risk, is well short of the 8/10 bar.
toReachEight: Fix mobile-ux-00 first (it's high severity and on the primary screen — distinct class name instead of reusing "hero"). Close the tap-target cluster as one pass rather than 8 separate patches: pick the 44px minimum the app already uses elsewhere (.acct-menu, .pl-brushes) and apply it uniformly to the Settings money inputs, the pay-period chip, Add-Shift shift-type chips, Pattern Lab grid cells and cycle-length buttons, the est-banner buttons, the avatar, and the day cells at ≤360px — then add a harness assertion that measures real hit-area on a representative set of these controls so the convention can't silently regress again (currently nothing in check_build.mjs or tests/smoke.mjs checks this, which is why it drifted this far). Route delGoal through confirmAsync like the differential delete. Add showShare to the scroll-lock effect. Wire the missing Enter-to-submit on the first-run swap-board inputs to match their later duplicates. Once those 11 confirmed items are closed and a regression guard exists, this lens clears 8; the 3 low-severity items (small-phone day cells, cycle buttons, onboarding autoFocus reintroducing an anti-pattern already fixed once in FeedbackSheet) are worth folding in but don't block the bar on their own.

worst: A systemic pattern, not one bug: the app's core interactive surfaces largely lack basic modal accessibility. AddShiftSheet (accessibility-10), PatternLab (accessibility-12), and Settings (accessibility-21) render as plain divs with no role="dialog"/aria-modal and no accessible name on their close buttons — "unlike every sibling sheet in the same file," per the findings. PatternLab additionally has zero focus trap and no Escape handler (accessibility-13), and SwapsSheet claims aria-modal="true" but has no focus trap, no initial focus, and no Escape handler either (accessibility-25) — so for a keyboard or screen-reader user, opening nearly any sheet in the app (Add-Shift, Pattern Lab, Settings, the swap board) either announces nothing or lets focus and Tab order leak straight into the obscured, supposedly-hidden app behind the overlay. Layered on top: onboarding — every new user's very first experience — never moves focus or uses heading markup across any of its 5 steps (accessibility-15), and the app's own OT/ESTIMATED tags on money figures fail AA contrast (accessibility-00, accessibility-16) in an app whose entire purpose is showing dollar figures.
toReachEight: Fix the systemic dialog gap first, since it recurs across most owned slices: give AddShiftSheet, PatternLab, Settings, and ShareSheet real role="dialog"/aria-modal plus a named close control (accessibility-02, -10, -12, -21, -22), and add a focus trap + Escape-to-close to PatternLab, SwapsSheet, and ConfirmHost to match the pattern the account menu already uses (accessibility-13, -25, -26). Fix the two confirmed AA contrast failures on money-adjacent text (accessibility-00 OT tag, accessibility-16 ESTIMATED tag) and the unverified-but-plausible ones flagged alongside them. Give onboarding focus movement and heading structure on every step transition (accessibility-15). Add aria-live to the live money readouts in Add-Shift and Pattern Lab (accessibility-03, -14), fix calendar grid semantics/keyboard scrollability (accessibility-04, -09) and the tablist-without-tab-pattern control (accessibility-06), and clean up the duplicate/missing accessible names (close buttons, Del buttons, differential-name input, unlabeled onboarding name field, back button — accessibility-02, -11, -18, -20, -23, -24). With 25 confirmed findings (10 high) across all 7 owned slices and none rejected, this is a real remediation project spanning most of the app's modals, not a couple of isolated patches — reaching 8 needs that whole set addressed, not just the highest-severity handful.

ranAgainst: docs/council-runs/2026-09-13/ranAgainst.json, performance:boot / performance:calendar / performance:pattern-lab / performance:data-sync slices — the boot script's 5 render-blocking cross-origin CDN <script> tags and the watchdog timing; App's calendar state/scroll machinery (monthWindow, onMonthScroll, focusRowDates, scrollFocusToDate), Calendar/MonthSection/YearList render, statOf/ptoStatOf; the debounced-save effect, pagehide flush, retrySync, and the 15s cross-device poll; pattern-lab's own bounded computation (cleared, no findings). worst: performance-00 (confirmed, medium): all 5 CDN scripts (React, ReactDOM, Babel standalone, pdf.js, supabase-js) are blocking <head> <script> tags across 3 third-party origins with no async/defer, so on a stalled hospital-WiFi connection the tab is blank white with zero feedback — not even the splash or the 8s watchdog — because the watchdog script itself can't run until all 5 resolve. toReachEight: Fix performance-00: move a tiny inline watchdog/loading-fallback to the very top of <head>, before the 5 blocking CDN scripts, so a stalled fetch on a filtered network still shows something within a couple seconds — independent of whether unpkg/cdnjs/jsdelivr ever respond. Those two together clear both confirmed findings. Separately (not required for 8, but real): the zero-React.memo fact behind the rejected performance-01/04 findings means the single-file/no-memoization architecture is still one Settings-keystroke or one cloud-save away from a visible stutter on an older iPhone with a full shift history — worth a follow-up session per CLAUDE.md's own "parked item" note, since a memo boundary on Calendar/MonthSection would make several of these findings moot at once.

worst: data-integrity-00 (confirmed, high) is still present in the current index.html: the pagehide/visibilitychange flush handler (2489-2505) calls saveToSupabase(...).then(ts=>{ if(ts){...} }) with no else branch, unlike the debounced save effect right above it (2476-2479) which calls writeBackup() on a failed save. This is the exact handler added because "500ms debounce would otherwise drop it" — so when a signed-in user edits a shift and immediately backgrounds or closes the tab on a flaky connection, the best-effort save can fail with zero recovery: no backup written, no syncError surfaced, nothing in memory once the tab is gone. Add a harness/unit assertion that simulates a failed saveToSupabase immediately followed by pagehide and confirms the edit survives via BACKUP_KEY and rehydrates on next load — this path has no test coverage today (infra slice confirmed nothing in tests/smoke.mjs touches sync/backup/MAX_BLOB_BYTES). Once that's shipped and re-reviewed clean, the six rejected races (01-06) already suggest the rest of the sync/import/backup design is sound, so this one fix plausibly clears the lens.
